name: Linux GPIO Number Converter
blurb: a SoC pin name to its gpiochip, line offset, legacy sysfs number and libgpiod commands
intro: Turns a SoC pin name (GPIO1_IO05, gpio1_28, PH5, GPIO3_B4, PA13, GPIO17 or a Raspberry Pi header pin) into the /dev/gpiochip it sits on, its line offset, the legacy sysfs number (chip base + offset) and the libgpiod v1/v2, sysfs and device-tree lines, from each SoC family's Linux driver numbering. It also works backwards from a sysfs number or chip:line.

inputs.label: Pin
inputs.placeholder: GPIO1_IO05, PH5, GPIO3_B4, GPIO17, pin 11, 117 or 3:20
inputs.help: A pin name, a legacy sysfs number, chip:line, or on a Raspberry Pi a header pin (pin 11).

inputs.label: Chip sysfs base
inputs.help: From /sys/class/gpio/gpiochip*/base on your board, when it differs from the historical default.

examples.title: Raspberry Pi 5, header pin 11, active-low button

usage: Give soc (imx6q, imx6ul, imx7d, imx8mm, am335x, h3, a64, rk3399, rk3568, rk3588, bcm2835, bcm2711, bcm2712, stm32mp15) and pin: a name in the SoC's own form (GPIO1_IO05, gpio1_28, PH5, GPIO3_B4, PA13, GPIO17), a legacy sysfs number, chip:line, or a Pi header pin ('pin 11'); optionally the chip's real sysfs base, the Pi kernel (new = 6.6+) and polarity. Returns the /dev/gpiochipN and label, line offset, sysfs number, the DT gpios specifier, a table of the SoC's chips, and texts with libgpiod v2/v1/sysfs commands and a DT snippet. Use it before writing a gpioset line, a sysfs export or a gpios property for a named pin.
sources: drivers/gpio/gpio-mxc.c, gpio-omap.c, gpio-rockchip.c; drivers/pinctrl/sunxi/pinctrl-sunxi.h (PL_BASE 352); drivers/pinctrl/stm32/pinctrl-stm32.c and stm32mp151.dtsi gpio-ranges
NXP i.MX6DQ/6UL/8MM reference manuals (GPIO bank sizes), Allwinner H3/A64 manuals (port pin counts)
Raspberry Pi documentation (40-pin header, BCM numbering); sysfs bases 0/512 and 399/571 as seen on Raspberry Pi OS kernels 6.1/6.6
libgpiod v1 and v2 tool man pages (gpioget, gpioset, gpioinfo, gpiomon)
